observations: A large face fills most of the canvas against a bright yellow field that shifts to olive-green in the lower half; a faint light-blue rectangle overlays the face's center.
Red-orange marks accent both eyes and the mouth, with a thick red stroke running from the lower lip down the chin; white teardrop shapes hang below each eye.
Loose black zigzag lines and orange blobs crowd the upper edge, echoing the jagged fringe that surrounds the face outline on the left side.
reading: Yellow floods the upper field while olive-green pools below, splitting the face across two tones of the same hue. White drops beneath each eye read as tears without insisting on it. Red at the mouth and eyes pulls against the yellow calm, and the faint blue rectangle floats over the face like a second, cooler layer. The result is one of contained pressure.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, title neighbors are nnxyz nnotb #295 and nnxyz nnotb #297. Where #295 builds its face on a saturated blue ground, #296 stays in yellow-to-olive — the scratched-line quality the collector relates to scrimshaw.

connections.reason: Both works anchor a face with bold black outline against a saturated single-color ground, but #295 floods that ground in blue while #296 stays yellow-olive, making the pair a direct color-temperature contrast on the same structural approach.

rawblocks #42 shares a bright yellow ground and a face built from layered lines, but buries its features under dense overlapping marks where #296 keeps the face relatively open, showing how the same yellow field can read as either noise or space.

lookingQuestion: Where exactly do the white shapes below the eyes begin and end, and what other marks in the image share their weight and color?
ambiguities: The faint light-blue rectangle overlaying the face may be a distinct drawn layer or a fill artifact; its edges are soft and its relationship to the face outline is unclear from the image alone.
Title-derived order and recorded-creation order align for this work, but gaps exist elsewhere in the owned nnotb subset, so adjacency does not confirm sequential making.
